parole.significato: A spicy and salty pickle in Indian cuisine.
parole.testo: From Hindustani اچار / अचार (acār), from Classical Persian آچار (āčār). Doublet of acar, atchara, and atsara.

parole.significato: A member of a Pashtun tribe.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani آفریدی (āfredī) / आफ़्रीदी (āfrīdī), from Pashto اپريدی (Apriday).

parole.significato: The leader of a pack of Cub Scouts.

parole.significato: Cupboard, cabinet or chest of drawers.

parole.significato: potato
parole.testo: From Hindustani آلو (ālo) / आलू (ālū), ultimately from Sanskrit आलु (ālu), said to mean the edible root of a variety of Amorphophallus paeoniifolius.

parole.significato: A bodice traditionally worn by Muslim women in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani انگیا / अंगिया (aṅgiyā), from Sanskrit अङ्गिका (aṅgikā).

parole.significato: An English person.
parole.testo: From Hindustani انگریز / अंग्रेज़ (aṅgrez), from Portuguese inglês (“Englishman”). Doublet of English.

parole.significato: Motherfucker (generic term of abuse).
parole.testo: Compound of aunt + fucker, by analogy with motherfucker. Calque of Hindustani خَالَہ چود (xāla cod) / ख़ालाचोद (xālācod).

parole.significato: Freedom, independence.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani آزادی (āzādī) / आज़ादी (āzādī), from Classical Persian آزادی (āzādī).

parole.significato: An almond.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani बादाम (bādām) / بادام (bādām) and other South Asian languages, from Classical Persian بادام (bādām), from Middle Persian wʾtʾm (wādām).

parole.significato: A rogue, ruffian or miscreant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani بدمعاش (badm'āś) / बदमाश (badmāś) and its source, Persian بدمعاش (badma'âš), from بد (bad, “bad, evil”) + معاش (ma'âš, “life, livelihood”), ultimately from Arabic عَاشَ (ʕāša, “to live”). Compare lowlife, which is a similar formation in English.

parole.significato: A wedding procession carried out by the bridegroom in North India, West India, and Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani بَرات (barāt) / बरात (barāt), ultimately from Sanskrit वरयात्रा (varayātrā).

parole.significato: An Indian dessert made from sweetened, condensed milk flavoured with fruit and spices.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani برفی / बर्फ़ी (barfī).

parole.significato: sisterfucker
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani بہن چود / बहनचोद (bahancod).

parole.significato: Property that is transacted under the name of a proxy to conceal the identity of the buyer.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani بے نامی (be nāmī) / बेनामी (benāmī, “nameless”), defined in the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act of 1988.

parole.significato: Indian: of, or relating to, the Republic of India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi भारतीय (bhāratīya), भारती (bhāratī) / Urdu بھارتی (bhāratī)). By surface analysis, Bharat + -i.

parole.significato: A crispy Indian snack made from moth beans, gram flour, and spices.
parole.testo: From Hindustani भुजिया / بھجیا (bhujiyā), ultimately from Sanskrit भृज्जति (bhṛjjati, “roasts, fries”). Related to fry and bhurji.

parole.significato: A spiced dish of rice, blended with meat and/or vegetables.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बिरयानी (biryānī) / Urdu بِرْیَانی (biryānī)), from Classical Persian بِرْیَانِی (biryānī), from بِرْیَان (biryān, “roast”) (from برشتن (birištan, “to roast”)) + the suffix ـی (-ī). Doublet of briam.

parole.significato: Motherfucker (generic term of abuse).
parole.testo: Compound of brother + fucker, after motherfucker. Calque of Hindustani بِرادَر چود (birādar cod) / बिरादरचोद (birādarcod).

parole.significato: A substitute in public or domestic service.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani बदली (badlī) / بَدلِی (badlī).

parole.significato: A system of discipline; organisation, arrangement, preparation.

parole.significato: A wandering grain and salt merchant in the Deccan Plateau (Southern India).

parole.significato: An honoured elder or superior.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बुज़ुर्ग (buzurg) / Urdu بُزُرْگ (buzurg), from Classical Persian بُزُرْگ (buzurg), from Middle Persian 𐭥𐭰𐭥𐭫𐭢 (wazurg, wuzurg), from Old Persian 𐎺𐏀𐎼𐎣 (vazạrka, “great, large”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wáȷ́rakas (“endowed with strength”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Eu

parole.significato: A breed of goat (Capra aegagrus hircus) raised for its hair.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani कश्मीर / کشمیر (kaśmīr, “Kashmir”), from Sanskrit कश्मीर (kaśmīra).

parole.significato: A long whip formerly used as an instrument of punishment in India and parts of the Middle East.
parole.testo: From Hindustani چابک / चाबुक (cābuk), from Classical Persian چابک (čābuk, “quick, swift; horsewhip”). Doublet of sjambok.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani چائے والا / चायवाला (cāyvālā); by surface analysis, chai + wallah.

parole.significato: Cannabis resin, used as an intoxicant in North India and Pakistan.

parole.significato: A screen or blind made of finely slit bamboo and twine, hung in doorways or windows.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi चिक़ (ciq) / Urdu چق (ciq)), ultimately from Classical Persian چق (čiq).

parole.significato: A conical pipe used for smoking marijuana, usually made of fired clay, porcelain, soapstone, glass or, more rarely, woo…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani चिलम (cilam) / چِلَم (cilam), from Classical Persian چِلَم (čilam).

parole.significato: A metal wash basin
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani चिलमची (cilamcī) / چِلَمْچِی (cilamcī).

parole.significato: An oriental plane tree (Platanus orientalis).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi चिनार (cinār) / Urdu چِنَار (cinār), in turn derived from Classical Persian چِنَار (činār, “Platanus”), ultimately derived from Middle Persian cynʾl (/⁠činār⁠/).

parole.significato: Keep quiet.
parole.testo: Anglo-Indian corruption of Hindustani चुप रहो / چُپ رَہو (cup raho, “Remain silent.”).

parole.significato: Sex, sexual intercourse, pornography.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani چُدائِی / चुदाई (cudāī, “sexual intercourse; prostitution”). Doublet of choad and choda.

parole.significato: A member of the Chuhra caste in India
parole.testo: From Hindustani چُوہْڑا (cūhṛā) / चूहड़ा (cūhṛā).

parole.significato: An island or shoal in a river.
parole.testo: From Hindustani چر / चर (car, “ford; island, shoal”).

parole.significato: A sweet or savory but usually spicy condiment, originally from eastern India, made from a variety of fruits and/or vege…

parole.significato: A measure of distance, varying from one and a quarter to two and a half English miles.

parole.significato: A clerk writing English.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani किरानी (kirānī) / کِرانِی (kirānī).

parole.significato: Someone whose net worth is greater than one crore (ten million) rupees or other local currency.

parole.significato: Making few demands; comfortable, easy.

parole.significato: A kind of cloth from India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani قُطْنِی (qutnī) / क़ुतनी (qutnī), from Classical Persian قطنى (qutnī).

parole.significato: A bandit or armed robber, especially in former parts of British India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani ڈکیت / डकैत (ḍakait), from ڈاکا (ḍākā) / डाका (ḍākā, “gang-robbery”).

parole.significato: Father’s father; paternal grandfather.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani दादाजी (dādājī).

parole.significato: A yogurt or fermented milk product.

parole.significato: A post system by means of transport relays of horses stationed at intervals along a route or network, carrying mail and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani डाक / ڈاک (ḍāk).

parole.significato: a drum having two heads opposite one another, commonly used in the Hindu and Buddhist religions.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi डमरू (ḍamrū) / Urdu ڈَمَرُو (ḍamarū)), Sanskrit डमरु (ḍamaru) and Tibetan ཌ་མ་རུ (ḍa ma ru).

parole.significato: Cinnamon.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani दारचीनी (dārcīnī) / دَارْچِینِی (dārcīnī).

parole.significato: A shrine associated with the grave of a Muslim saint or similar religious figure.
parole.testo: From Hindustani درگاہ / दरगाह (dargāh), from Classical Persian درگاه (dargāh). See also English eidgah.

parole.significato: Not at home; currently unwilling to receive visitors into one's house.
parole.testo: From Hindustani دروازہ / दरवाज़ा (darvāzā) + بند / बंद (band).

parole.significato: A commission or duty charged by an agent; a kickback.

parole.significato: A South Asian type of cooking pot used to store biryani to keep it warm.
parole.testo: From Hindustani دیگچی / देगची (degcī).

parole.significato: A look; a glance.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani देखो / دیکھو (dekho), imperative of देखना / دیکھنا (dekhnā, “to see, to look”).

parole.significato: Belonging to a certain revivalist movement within Sunni Islam.
parole.testo: From Hindustani دیوبندی / देवबन्दी (devbandī); which means "of Deoband, Deobandi," from Devband, Deoband, town in Uttar Pradesh, India, the location of the Islamic seminary in which the movement began.

parole.significato: Any member of the species Cedrus deodara of cedar trees native to the western Himalayas.
parole.testo: Borrowed from colloquial Hindustani دیودار (dyodār) / देओदार (deodār), from دیودار (dyodār) / देवदार (devdār), from Sanskrit देवदारु (deva-dāru, literally “divine tree”).

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to the culture, people, or products of South Asia; South Asian.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani دیسی (desī) / देसी (desī).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani دُون (dūn) / दून (dūn).

parole.significato: A bowed string instrument of Indian origin, with a goatskin soundboard, sympathetic strings and twenty frets
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani دلربا / दिलरुबा (dilrubā).

parole.significato: A double layer of cloth worn by women as a scarf, veil etc.

parole.significato: A ceremonial gathering held by a ruler in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani دربار / दरबार (darbār), in turn borrowed from Classical Persian دربار (darbār, “royal court”).

parole.significato: A live-in doorkeeper, especially in an apartment building.
parole.testo: From Hindustani دروان (drvān) / दरवान (darvān), from Classical Persian دروان (darwān), from دربان (darbān, “doorkeeper”), from در (dar, “door”) + ـبان (-bān, “keeper, guardian”).

parole.significato: A tailor, especially a personal one.
parole.testo: From Hindustani درزی / दर्ज़ी (darzī, “tailor”), from Persian درزی (darzi, “tailor”).

parole.significato: cardamom
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi इलायची (ilāycī) / Urdu اِلائِچی (ilāicī)), from Middle Hindi, from Old Hindi, from Sauraseni Prakrit, from Prakrit, ultimately from Proto-South Dravidian *ēlVkkāy. Related to Sanskrit एलीका (elīkā), Classical Persian هیل (hēl).

parole.significato: A generic term of abuse, similar to motherfucker.
parole.testo: Compound of father + fucker. Calque of Hindustani پِدَر چود (pidar cod) / पिदरचोद (pidarcod).

parole.significato: Army.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani فَوج (fauj) / फ़ौज (fauj), from Classical Persian فَوْج (fawj), from Arabic فَوْج (fawj).

parole.significato: A foreigner, especially a British or a white person.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani फ़िरंगी (firaṅgī) / فرنگی (firangī), from Classical Persian فرنگی (farangī), from Old French franc. Doublet of franc.

parole.significato: An alleyway or side street.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani گَلی (galī) / गली (galī).

parole.significato: An arsehole, an idiot.
parole.testo: From Hindustani گانڈو / गांडू (gāṇḍū).

parole.significato: A traditional garment of Lucknow in India, consisting of kurti, dupatta, and wide-legged flaring trousers which are oft…
parole.testo: From Hindustani غراره / ग़रारा (ġarārā).

parole.significato: A type of clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani گھی (ghī) / घी (ghī), traditionally explained as from Sanskrit घृत (ghṛta, “sprinkled”) (See घृत entry 3 for details). First attested in the late 17th century.

parole.significato: Pertaining to a fair-skinned or European person.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani Hindi गोरा (gorā) / Urdu گورا (gorā). * In British Pakistani speech, influenced also by Pahari-Potwari گورا (gorā) and Punjabi ਗੋਰਾ (gorā) / گورا (gorā).

parole.significato: A South Asian dessert made from milk solids that are deep-fried and soaked in syrup.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani گلاب جامن / गुलाब जामुन (gulāb jāmun), from गुलाब (gulāb, “rosewater”), in turn from Classical Persian گُلَاب (gulāb), from گُل (gul, “rose”) + آب (āb, “water”), and जामुन (jāmun, “jambul”).

parole.significato: A competition where riders and horses display a range of skills and aptitudes.
parole.testo: From Hindustani گیند خانہ (gendxānā) / गेंदख़ाना (gendxānā, “racquet court”), from گیند / गेंद (gend, “ball”) + خانہ / ख़ाना (xānā, “court”). Influenced by gymnastics and gymnasium.

parole.significato: A kind of dwarf cow bred in Bengal.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani گَینِی (gainī) - गैनी (gainī).

parole.significato: A member of an ethnic group of North India and Pakistan, traditionally working as barbers.
parole.testo: From Hindustani حجام / हज्जाम (hajjām, “barber”), from Classical Persian حجام (hajjām), from Arabic حَجَّام (ḥajjām).

parole.significato: A doctor, usually practicing traditional medicine.
parole.testo: From Hindustani حکیم / हकीम (hakīm), from Classical Persian حکیم (hakīm), from Arabic حَكِيم (ḥakīm, “wise, learned”).

parole.significato: A grain.

parole.significato: a Christian.
parole.testo: From Hindustani عیسائی/ईसाई (īsāī, “people of Jesus”), from Arabic عِيسَى (ʕīsā, “Jesus”).

parole.significato: Honour, pride; reputation.

parole.significato: One who holds a jagir.

parole.significato: a kind of duet in Indian classical music.

parole.significato: Visceral leishmaniasis.

parole.significato: An artist.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani कलाकार (kalākār) / کَلَاکَار (kalākār).

parole.significato: A canvas screen or partition forming the wall or division of a tent or other enclosure.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani क़नात (qanāt, “wall of tent; canvas screen”).

parole.significato: A record keeper involved in the administration of the pargana.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani कारकुन (kārkun) / کارکن, from Classical Persian کار کن (kār-kun, “worker”).

parole.significato: An Indian push dagger with an H-shaped handle, used predominantly ceremonially, and rarely as a weapon.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani کَٹَار (kaṭār) / कटार (kaṭār, “dagger, saber”).

parole.significato: Saffron.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani केसर / کیسر (kesar, “saffron”), from Sanskrit केसर (késara).

parole.significato: food, a meal

parole.significato: A plot of land.

parole.significato: A male servant, with responsibility for waiting at table.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani خدمتگار (xidmatgār) / ख़िदमतगार, from Classical Persian خدمتگار (xidmatgār).

parole.significato: A curry made from various spices especially coriander and cumin; and often with yoghurt sauce or nuts.

parole.significato: One hundred thousand (10⁵): 100,000, that is, with Indian digit grouping, 1,00,000.

parole.significato: A Sufi devotional poem in praise of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the son-in-law of Muhammad, or of any Sufi saint.

parole.significato: A soft, non-matured, Indian cheese.

parole.significato: An Indian bread with a texture somewhat resembling puff pastry; sometimes stuffed with vegetables etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani पराठा (parāṭhā) / پَراٹھا (parāṭhā). Doublet of parotta.

parole.significato: Synonym of Pashtun; a member of the Pashto-speaking people of today’s north-west Pakistan and south-east Afghanistan.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani पेशगी (peśgī) / پیشْگی (peśgī, “advance”).

parole.significato: A mattock or large hoe.

parole.significato: To seize; to take hold of.

parole.significato: Spring.

parole.significato: A workman who repairs shawls and other woolen fabrics; a darner.

parole.significato: The wife of a rajah.
parole.testo: From Hindustani رانی (rānī) / रानी (rānī), from Sanskrit राज्ञी (rā́jñī, “queen, princess”). Doublet of Regina.

parole.significato: A coverlet quilted with cotton.

parole.significato: A square or rectangular piece of cloth worn as a covering for the head, neck, and shoulders, typically by women.

parole.significato: Any tree of the genus Albizia.

parole.significato: An extremely undesirable person.
parole.testo: Compound of sister + fucker. Calque of Hindustani بہن چود / बहनचोद (bahancod).

parole.significato: One who engages in incest with their son.
parole.testo: Compound of son + fucker, by analogy with motherfucker. Calque of Hindustani بیٹا چود (beṭā cod) / बेटाचोद (beṭācod).

parole.significato: A pair of tuned hand drums, used in various musical genres of the Indian subcontinent, that are similar to bongos.
parole.testo: From Hindustani طبلہ / तबला (tablā), from Arabic طَبْلَة (ṭabla). Cognate of Catalan, Spanish, Portuguese tambor.

parole.significato: A cylindrical clay oven used in the cuisine of the Caucasus, Middle East, and Indian subcontinent to make flat bread or…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani तंदूर (tandūr) / تندور (tandūr), from Classical Persian تنور (tannūr), from Middle Persian [script needed] (tnwl /⁠tanūr⁠/, “oven”), ultimately from Akkadian 𒋾𒂟 (tinūru), all meaning "(clay) oven". Compare also Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬥𐬏𐬭𐬀 (tanūra). Doublet of athanor.

parole.significato: Cooked in a tandoor.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani तन्दूरी (tandūrī) / تندوری (tandūrī), from Classical Persian تنوری (tanūrī).

parole.significato: Heated oil or ghee in which spices and onion, etc. are well-stirred and browned.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani तड़का / تڑکا (taṛkā).

parole.significato: A professional courtesan serving the nobility, especially under the Mughal Empire; (derogatory)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi तवायफ़ (tavāyaf) / Urdu طَوائِف (tavāif)), in turn derived from Classical Persian طَوَائِف (tawā'if), ultimately derived from Arabic طَوائِف (ṭawāʔif).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: A person who is a member of a gang or criminal organization.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani ठग (ṭhag) / ٹھگ (ṭhag, “swindler, fraud, cheat”), further derived from Prakrit 𑀞𑀕 (ṭhaga), of uncertain origin. See there for more. Thuggee was a network of gangs in India from the 17th century to the 19th century who robbed and murdered travellers, often by strangling. Duri

parole.significato: A thug (a member of band of assassins in India).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani ठगी (ṭhagī) / ٹھگی (ṭhagī).

parole.significato: A marinade made from various aromatic spices usually with a yoghurt base; often used in Indian cuisine prior to grillin…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani टिक्का (ṭikkā, “piece”) / ٹِکّہ (ṭikka), ultimately from Classical Persian تکه (tikka).

parole.significato: A term of abuse, variant of motherfucker.
parole.testo: Compound of uncle + fucker, by analogy with motherfucker. Calque of Hindustani خَالُو چود (xālū cod) / ख़ालूचोद (xālūcod). Popularised by the song "Uncle Fucka" in South Park: Bigger, Longer, Uncut, a 1999 American adult-animated comedy film.

parole.significato: Of or relating to the Urdu language.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (see Urdu اُرْدُو (urdū) and Hindi उर्दू (urdū)), from Classical Persian اُرْدُو (urdū), from Proto-Turkic *ordu (“army, camp”) ( > Azerbaijani ordu, Turkish ordu, Turkmen oorda). Doublet of horde and orda.

parole.significato: A Mughal land revenue system that replaced the earlier tribute system with a monetary tax system based on a uniform cur…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani ज़ब्त (zabt)/ضَبْط (zabt), from Classical Persian ضبط (zabt), from Arabic ضَبْط (ḍabṭ).

parole.significato: Saffron.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani زَعْفَرانی (zaʻfarānī, “saffrony”) / ज़ाफ़रानी (zāfrānī), from Classical Persian زعفرانی (za'frāni, “saffrony”), from زعفران (za'frân, “saffron”).

parole.significato: Long live.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani ज़िंदाबाद (zindābād) / زندہ باد (zinda bād, “long live”), from Classical Persian زنده باد (zinda bād).

parole.significato: A storage room or armoury where firearms and magazines are kept.
parole.testo: From arms + possibly Punjabi ਕੋਟ (koṭ, “fort”) or Hindustani کوٹ / कोट (koṭ, “fort, barracks”), ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *kōṭṭay (“wall”). Compare Tamil கோட்டை (kōṭṭai, “fort, castle, stronghold”). Alternatively, from Hindi कोठा (koṭhā, “warehouse”) or a related cognate. First used in British

parole.significato: A literal or metaphorical force or object regarded as unstoppable, that will crush all in its path.
parole.testo: Borrowed in the 17th century into British English in India, either through Hindustani جَگَنَّاتھ (jagannāth) / जगन्नाथ (jagannāth) or directly from Odia ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (jagannātha), ultimately from Sanskrit ज॒ग॒न्ना॒थ (jagannāthá, “lord of universe”) (Jagannatha), a title for the Hindu deity Vishnu's avata
